name: agent-essential-skills
description: One install for the 10 open-source tools that give native AI agents real context.

tools.name: claude-mem
tools.why: Native agents forget everything between sessions. This gives them memory.
tools.does: Captures what your agent did, compresses it, and injects useful past context into the next session.

install.notes: Interactive installer. Pick Cursor and/or Claude Code when prompted.

tools.name: context7
tools.why: Agents guess APIs from stale training data. This feeds them live docs.
tools.does: Pulls up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples into the agent.

install.notes: Setup can install skill and/or MCP. Full use needs a free Context7 API key — see docs/KEYS.md.

tools.name: graphify
tools.why: Grepping a big codebase burns tokens and still misses structure. A graph is searchable context.
tools.does: Turns a codebase into a queryable knowledge graph (query / path / explain) so agents get scoped answers.

install.skill: npx skills add Graphify-Labs/graphify -g -a cursor -a claude-code -y
install.notes: After install, run `graphify .` inside a project.

tools.name: ponytail
tools.why: Agents over-engineer by default. This forces the laziest solution that still works.
tools.does: Skill that pushes YAGNI, stdlib-first, fewer dependencies, and minimal diffs.

install.skill: npx skills add DietrichGebert/ponytail -g -a cursor -a claude-code -y

tools.name: playwright-mcp
tools.why: Without a browser, an agent cannot verify the UI it just built.
tools.does: MCP server that lets the agent navigate, click, type, and snapshot pages via Playwright.

install.notes: Wired into Cursor and Claude Code MCP config by install.sh.

tools.name: superpowers
tools.why: Agents jump straight into code. This makes them brainstorm, plan, test, and review first.
tools.does: Composable skills for brainstorming, planning, TDD, subagent execution, and code review.

install.skill: npx skills add obra/superpowers -g -a cursor -a claude-code -y
install.notes: Skills path works for Cursor + Claude Code. Claude Code can also use the official plugin.

tools.name: repomix
tools.why: Sometimes you need the whole repo in one AI-friendly file, not a live graph.
tools.does: Packs a repository into a single XML/markdown file with token counts, ignores, and optional compression.

install.skill: npx skills add yamadashy/repomix -g -a cursor -a claude-code -y

tools.name: firecrawl
tools.why: Agents are blind to the live web unless you give them a scrape/search tool.
tools.does: Search, scrape, and crawl the web into clean markdown/JSON for agents.

install.notes: MCP is wired by install.sh. Most features need a Firecrawl API key — see docs/KEYS.md.

tools.name: serena
tools.why: Raw file search is slow and clumsy in large codebases. Symbol-level tools are how an IDE works.
tools.does: MCP server with IDE-like semantic retrieval and editing (find symbol, references, rename) via language servers.

install.notes: Wired into MCP config by install.sh after the CLI is installed.

tools.name: caveman
tools.why: Agents waste tokens on filler. Shorter prose leaves more room for code and tools.
tools.does: Skill that makes the agent answer densely (less hedging and ceremony) while keeping code and errors exact.

install.skill: npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g -a cursor -a claude-code -y

tools.caveat: Token savings are real on chatty answers; on coding-agent work they are usually much smaller than marketing claims.
